item.description: Follow along with the latest NFL news and injury updates approaching Week 1.
item.content:encoded:
The NFL season is now underway.

The Seattle Seahawks, even after losing quarterback Sam Darnold to a hip injury, rallied back to beat the New England Patriots 13-10 on Wednesday night in a rematch of Super Bowl LX.

The team believes it avoided a worst-case scenario with Darnold, though the quarterback could still miss multiple weeks due to the injury. He’ll undergo an MRI on Thursday.

From @GMFB: #Seahawks QB Sam Darnold (hip) awaits results of his MRI today, but overall the initial results were encouraging. Short-term IR is still a possibility. pic.twitter.com/m7jZElPaDb

— Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) September 10, 2026

Leading up to that matchup, the Patriots agreed to a record-setting four-year, $135 million extension with star cornerback Christian Gonzalez, resetting the cornerback market yet again this offseason. While their defense was solid, Drake Maye threw three interceptions in the loss for the Patriots. That's not a great start to the year.

With that now in the books, attention will now turn to the first ever matchup in Australia on Thursday night. The Los Angeles Rams and San Francisco 49ers will square off on Netflix to keep the season moving.

Reigning Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett will make his debut with the franchise after his blockbuster trade from the Cleveland Browns earlier this offseason. He's missed practice time in training camp and through the preseason with knee swelling but should be good to go. Fans will have to wait at least another week to see the recently unretired Aaron Donald make his return, however, after he didn't travel with the team to Melbourne.

Gonzalez wasn't the only player who benefited from a massive payday this week. After it appeared as though Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield would have to play the 2026 campaign on the final year of his contract, he received a last-minute extension, days before the Bucs take on the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 1. Tampa Bay inked the two-time Pro Bowler to a three-year, $165 million contract that takes him through the 2029 season.

item.title: Sam Darnold ruled out with hip injury after only one drive, replaced by Drew Lock in Seahawks win
item.description: Sam Darnold was sacked and suffered a leg injury early in Wednesday's game.
item.content:encoded:
The Seattle Seahawks' celebration over raising their Super Bowl banner and the start of a new season didn't last long Wednesday.

Quarterback Sam Darnold left the season-opening game against the New England Patriots after one series due to a hip injury. He was replaced by Drew Lock. Darnold went back to the locker room with athletic trainers before the Seahawks' second series started.

Late in the second quarter, Darnold was ruled out by the Seahawks for the rest of the game. After a slow start, Lock and Seattle made just enough plays to pull off a dramatic 13-10 win.

Darnold was not at the stadium for the rest of the game. He went to nearby Harborview Medical Center for a CT scan on his hip, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter. That test came back inconclusive, and he's set to undergo an MRI on Thursday. After the game, Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said he believes a fracture has been ruled out, per ESPN.

"At this point, we are able to rule out a fracture," Macdonald said. "So there's some more tests to be done. ... We're still working through all that, but right now I think fracture is out, which is great news."

While the Seahawks believe they avoided a worst-case scenario, short-term IR is reportedly possible, per NFL Network.

From @GMFB: #Seahawks QB Sam Darnold (hip) awaits results of his MRI today, but overall the initial results were encouraging. Short-term IR is still a possibility. pic.twitter.com/m7jZElPaDb

— Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) September 10, 2026

Lock finished 16 of 22 for 187 yards passing and a 45-yard touchdown pass to Jaxon Smith-Njigba.

On the play he was hurt, Darnold was sacked by Patriots end Dre'Mont Jones on a third down on the Seahawks' first drive. As the punt team came on, Darnold was trotting off with a noticeable limp. NBC said on the broadcast that no medical personnel was around Darnold as he came to the sideline, but shortly after he went to the blue medical tent.

Sam Darnold is questionable to return with HIP injury, per press box announcer. Back in tunnel getting X-rays as Drew Lock plays in relief. https://t.co/HgsTN771xr

— Jori Epstein (@JoriEpstein) September 10, 2026

After the Patriots punted, NBC showed Darnold limping badly on the sideline as Lock had his helmet on, ready to go in.

Darnold didn't miss a game last season and threw for 4,000 yards in the regular season, then played steady, solid football throughout the Seahawks' Super Bowl championship push. He became a great story of a highly drafted quarterback who was given up on by multiple teams.

As a new season started, another story was unfolding and it wasn't a positive one for the Seahawks or Darnold.

item.title: Can new-look Titans defense force Jets QB Geno Smith into mistakes?
item.description: Can Robert Saleh’s Tennessee Titans defense force New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith into Week 1 mistakes?
item.content:encoded:
Tennessee Titans head coach Robert Saleh will officially begin his era on Sunday. The Titans are hosting the New York Jets in their Week 1 opener of the 2026 NFL season. Coach Saleh will be debuting his new-look defense.

Saleh is a defensive-minded coach. General manager Mike Borgonzi built the defense in his vision. Saleh was especially allowed to revamp the defensive line, acquiring players he had coached before like Jermaine Johnson II, John Franklin-Myers, Solomon Thomas, Jacob Martin, and Jordan Elliott.

One area of emphasis for this new-look Titans defense is 2026 will be to force more turnovers. The 2025 Titans were -5 in turnover differential last year. They notched just 14 total takeaways, tied for fourth-last in the NFL. They only had six interceptions, third-fewest.

New Jets starting quarterback Geno Smith is a gunslinger. He led the league in interceptions throughout the 2025 season with 17 despite playing just 15 games. In 2024, Smith’s 15 interceptions were tied for second-most in the NFL. He loves testing tight throwing windows.

The Jets have weapons. Garrett Wilson and Breece Hall are proven playmakers. They used two first-round picks on a pair of rookie pass catchers in Kenyon Sadiq and Omar Cooper Jr. They also expect Mason Taylor and Adonai Mitchell to continue getting better. Smith will attempt to sling the ball around.

Saleh’s San Francisco 49ers defense also struggled to record interceptions last year. They actually tied the Titans with six. We’ll see if acquisitions like Cor’Dale Flott and Alontae Taylor help. Safety Amani Hooker uncharacteristically had zero interceptions in 2025 after registering a career-high five in 2024.

Saleh brought his aggressive defense to the Titans. Hopefully it yields better results in the turnover department. The Titans will see a mistake-prone Smith at quarterback in Week 1. Hopefully the new approach pays dividends.

item.title: Bold predictions for Rams-49ers 2026 season opener
item.description: 5 bold predictions for the Rams season opener in Australia
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Rams and San Francisco 49ers are set to make NFL history when they meet at the Melbourne Cricket Ground in Australia for the first-ever regular-season NFL game played in the country. The Week 1 matchup brings one of the league’s most familiar rivalries to an entirely unfamiliar setting, creating a unique backdrop for the start of the 2026 season.

Beyond the history and international spotlight, the game presents a fascinating football challenge for both teams. The two organizations have taken drastically different approaches to preparing for the trip. San Francisco arrived in Melbourne roughly a week before kickoff to acclimate to the time difference, while the Rams elected to maintain their normal routine and travel much closer to game day.

The Rams enter the matchup as 3.5-point favorites, according to the FanDuel betting spread, adding another layer of intrigue to an already highly anticipated NFC West showdown. Los Angeles will look to begin the season with a statement victory, while San Francisco will attempt to spoil the Rams’ historic international home game. With much anticipation going into the Rams season, here are five bold predictions for tonight’s game…

1. Braden Fiske collects 2 sacks

The Rams defense has a whole will collect 4 sacks but Fiske will be the man that sets the tone with Aaron Donald declared inactive. Fiske enters year three with a high ceiling considering the Rams defensive prowess. Kyle Shanahan will likely focus a lot of attention on Myles Garrett; giving Fiske the opportunity to win his 1 on 1s.

2. Rams rush for 175+ yards

With Raheem Morris determined to take away Matthew Stafford, Sean McVay sets the tone on the ground with the tandem of Kyren Williams and Blake Corum. The 49ers defensive front that is working its way back from past and current injuries can’t handle the Rams decision to attack on the ground out of 12 and 13 personnel.

3. First touchdown of the year: Terrance Ferguson

Second year tight end will be the first Ram to find the end zone; hauling in a 17 yard pass from Matthew Stafford to get the Rams first touchdown of the season and the first touchdown in Melbourne, Australia.

4. McCaffrey rushes for less than 60 yards

The Rams “fearsome foursome” earns its name in the opener; bottling up Christian McCaffrey to under 60 yards on the ground. McCaffrey still receives touches in the passing game but the Rams defensive front does its job; making the 49ers one dimensional.

5. Harrison Mevis drills 4 field goals

The Rams special teams woes in 2025 really haunted them from the beginning of 2025 till the end. Harrison Mevis however brought stability to the place kicker position after the team cut Joshua Karty. Mevis starts off the 2026 season with a memorable performance; connecting on 4 field goals to help propel the Rams to victory.

item.title: How long is Sam Darnold out? Injury update, return date for Seahawks QB
item.description: Sam Darnold suffered a hip injury in the Seahawks' Week 1 win over the Patriots. Here's how long that injury will sideline the veteran QB.
item.content:encoded:
The Seattle Seahawks came from behind to earn a 13-10 win in their 2026 season opener against the New England Patriots.

Seattle's victory came at the expense of their starting quarterback, Sam Darnold, who was injured early during the proceedings.

Darnold was sacked by Patriots edge rusher Dre'Mont Jones on Seattle's fifth offensive snap of the game. The 29-year-old quarterback was helped to his feet by his teammates but was seen limping as he exited the field.

Darnold originally sat on the bench upon reaching the sideline but later retreated to the blue medical tent. He was then taken back to the locker room for additional examination before being ruled out for the remainder of the game with a hip injury.

Now, the Seahawks will await news on Darnold's status as they look to defend their Super Bowl 60 title.

Here's what to know about Darnold's injury and when he might return to action.

Sam Darnold injury update

The Seahawks announced Darnold had been ruled out for the remainder of their 2026 season opener just before halftime. He had previously been "questionable" to return because of a hip injury.

Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald provided a positive update about Darnold's status after the game. Initial tests revealed the quarterback had not suffered a fractured hip.

"There's some more tests to be done, so that's what I'm saying when it's positive," Macdonald told reporters. "I know we're still working through all that, but right now, I think fracture's out, which is great news."

Darnold will have additional testing to determine the extent of his injury.

How long is Sam Darnold out?

The Seahawks did not immediately announce a timetable for Darnold's return.

Macdonald was asked whether he had any hope Darnold would be able to play in the team's Week 2 game against the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday, Sept. 20. His response?

"I really don't know. I don't know what the extent is," Macdonald said, referencing Darnold's injury. "I don't know."

Who is Sam Darnold's backup?

Drew Lock is the Seahawks' backup quarterback. The 29-year-old performed well in Darnold's stead against the Patriots, completing 16 of 22 passes for 187 yards and a touchdown. He also added 13 yards on two carries, one of which was a 14-yard scramble.

Lock was originally a second-round pick by the Denver Broncos in the 2019 NFL Draft. He entered play Wednesday with a career record of 10-18 in 28 career starts and has completed 59.6% of his career passes for 6,369 yards, 34 touchdowns and 28 interceptions.

Seahawks QB depth chart

The Seahawks have three quarterbacks on their 53-man roster. Below is a look at the pecking order within that unit:

  1. Sam Darnold
  2. Drew Lock
  3. Jalen Milroe

Milroe, a third-round pick in 2025, played sparingly during his rookie season. He logged three carries for four yards while playing in three games. The Alabama product did not attempt a pass and spent most of his season in the emergency third-string role.

item.title: Seahawks just put Rams, NFL on notice
item.description: The NFL season has begun, the Los Angeles Rams play tonight and more news to check out!
item.content:encoded:
The Seattle Seahawks may not have dominated the New England Patriots solely based on their winning score of 13-10, but if you watched the game, then you saw the Seahawks overcome an injury to their starting quarterback, you saw them overcome a 10-0 deficit, you saw their defense fight the entire game, you saw their defense takeover late in the contest with 3 interceptions, you saw Mike Macdonald continue to establish himself as one of the best coaches in the NFL.

It was all on display Wednesday night for Seattle, and they showed the entire league that they are back in 2026 like they never left after their February Super Bowl victory.

It’s one game, heard, but it’s all we have to go off of.

Right now, the Seahawks look like the best team in the NFL. The Patriots look ready for a major regression for their successful 2025 season.

Plenty of games to go to change all the narratives, including a game tonight between the Los Angeles Rams and the San Francisco 49ers in Australia. What narratives will there be after tonight’s show?

Tune in, find out.

Seahawks rally over Patriots: Seattle capitalizes on three fourth-quarter interceptions from Drake Maye (cbsports)

“Sam Darnold exited after five plays with a hip injury and did not return, and the Seahawks committed nearly 100 yards’ worth of penalties, but somehow, some way, Seattle rallied past New England, 13-10, in a Super Bowl LX rematch slugfest. The Seahawks’ defense picked off Drake Maye three times in the fourth quarter, with Josh Jobe sealing the game on an absolutely baffling throw by Maye when New England was in field goal range.“

Niners vs. Rams: Three must-know storylines for NFL’s first-ever game in Australia (nfl.com)

“The 49ers-Rams season opener promises to be one for the history books — not just because it’s the first regular-season NFL contest to be played in Australia, or that it’ll take place at a 172-year-old cricket ground (nearly a Belichick older than Soldier Field), or that it could begin on a Friday and end on a Thursday (time zones, maaaaan).

More simply, this clash between the California rivals is set to stand out more for what happens on the pitch than off it.

Los Angeles, the reigning NFC runner-up, loaded up on star power ahead of SoFi Stadium’s second Super Bowl-hosting gig. Jaylen Watson. Trent McDuffie. Myles Garrett. Aaron Donald. They’re all wearing Royal and Sol these days. So too are returning stars Matthew Stafford, Puka Nacua and Davante Adams.

It’s as stacked a cast as we’ve seen in Hollywood since Ocean’s Eleven. Will Sean McVay’s 11 get off on the right foot in Week 1? Their old nemeses from up north are in the way.“

Rams’ 5 keys to victory against the 49ers in Week 1 (ramswire)

“The Los Angeles Rams are set to face the San Francisco 49ers on Thursday night, kicking off what should be one of the league’s best games this season. If the Rams are to leave Melbourne with a win, here are five keys to taking down the Niners.

Work Nick Bosa into obscurity

Bosa is set to play and is without a doubt the 49ers’ best pass rusher. The 49ers also made one of the most underrated roster moves of the offseason, adding defensive tackle Osa Odighizuwa, who will play a big role in helping them control the line of scrimmage.“

Shawne Merriman says Rams’ Aaron Donald-Myles Garrett combo is ‘insane’ for NFL offenses: ‘Pick your poison’ (foxnews)

“The expectations and potential of what this combo could do to offenses in 2026 has got football players, coaches and fans in a collective whirlwind. And one former NFL star linebacker thinks the hype couldn’t be more real.

“Just insane. I mean, it’s insane because every week will be a pick-your-poison situation,” Shawne Merriman, All-Pro linebacker for the San Diego Chargers and Buffalo Bills, told OutKick in a recent interview. “Who do you want to focus on? Because the other one is going to make plays.”

LA Rams President Kevin Demoff touts Australia push ahead of historic NFL game (cnbc.com)

“Demoff said the Rams own the rights to seven international markets, mostly in the Pacific Rim, and that Australia has felt like a natural fit.

“Being a global city in Los Angeles, it’s important to tap into those roots,” he said. “When you think about Australia, everybody here flies over SoFi Stadium in Hollywood Park, [California,] as they come to the U.S. to enter to go to any other global destination.”

How to Watch 49ers vs. Rams: TV Channel, Live Stream, Time (foxsports)

“The San Francisco 49ers and Los Angeles Rams meet Thursday, Sept. 10, 2026, in a first for the league: a regular-season game at Melbourne Cricket Ground in Melbourne, Australia, with kickoff set for 8:35 p.m. ET.”

Rams-49ers injury report: Game statuses for Garrett, Watson and Kittle (ramswire)

“After holding a light practice in Melbourne, the Los Angeles Rams released their final injury report of Week 1. Given the lack of health concerns entering the week, it’s no surprise that the Rams are in excellent shape for the season opener against the San Francisco 49ers.

Aaron Donald is the only player with an injury designation after being ruled out on Tuesday. He did not make the trip to Australia with the team, staying back in Los Angeles in hopes of being ready to play sooner rather than later.“

The NFL season has begun, the Los Angeles Rams play tonight and more news to check out! (sports.yahoo)

“But the biggest bad news for the head coach Sean McVay and the squad is that their veteran defender Aaron Donald won’t be going to Australia due to injury and is ruled out for this game.

Meanwhile, 32-year-old Kittle has been playing in the NFL since 2017. He has recorded 8,008 yards in 124 games and scored 52 touchdowns. Even in the last season before getting injured, he scored 7 touchdowns in 11 games, showing just how much of a game-winning player he is.

The 49ers’ head coach Kyle Shanahan said that Kittle and another key defender, Nick Bosa, are both coming back after major injuries.“

Vivid Seats Becomes Official Fan Experience Partner of Los Angeles Rams (ticketnews)

“Geoff Lester, chief commercial officer at Vivid Seats, said the partnership is intended to provide fans with additional opportunities to engage with live sports.

“We’re thrilled to partner with the Los Angeles Rams,” Lester said. “We’re always looking for new ways to make live events more rewarding and memorable for fans.”

He added that the agreement will combine the enthusiasm of Rams supporters with access to experiences at SoFi Stadium.“

Rams and Niners battle in first-ever NFL game Down Under | Game Preview (rams.com)

“As we know, the Rams were a play away from hosting the NFC Championship Game in 2024.

They were a play away from winning the NFC Championship Game in 2025.

However, that doesn’t mean they’re a play away from winning another World Championship at SoFi Stadium.

There are so many blocks to stack between here and there, and we know that progress isn’t linear in the NFL.

That’s a good thing for your Los Angeles Rams. Because the goal isn’t to reach Super Bowl LXI – it’s to win it.“

Comment of the Day:

“I thought Maye had a lot to prove this year. I didn’t know that the splits were so stark. 0-12 against winning teams? That’s not an aberration, that’s a trend. The way he played in the 4th quarter last night said it all.”-delusionalramfanslosteve

item.title: Drake Maye calls game-sealing interception 'unacceptable,' vows to be better after rough Week 1
item.description: All three of the Patriots' fourth-quarter drives ended in interceptions.
item.content:encoded:
With roughly 30 seconds to go Wednesday, the New England Patriots seemed like a lock to — at least — force overtime against the defending champion Seattle Seahawks. But instead of throwing the ball away on the next play, quarterback Drake Maye took an ill-advised shot at the end zone.

It cost his team. For the third time during the contest, Maye was intercepted. This one wound up sealing the victory for the Seahawks, who narrowly won 13-10 in Week 1.

While the Patriots showed a handful of concerning trends during the contest, Maye bore the brunt of the ire after throwing interceptions on each of the Patriots' final three drives of the night. The first came with the team trying to hold a lead, the second came with the game tied and the third came with the team already in position for a game-tying field goal.

After the contest, Maye called his final interception "unacceptable," and said his performance Wednesday "wasn't how I play football and how I want to represent my game," per ESPN.

Maye vowed to be better moving forward.

"I vow to myself to be better and realize it's a long season. But at the same time, you can't have those. It's unacceptable."

After the contest, Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel echoed that sentiment, saying he wants Maye to be "aggressive, not reckless" in those situations. Vrabel later added, "You can't throw three interceptions. Drake knows that."

It was a disappointing performance from Maye, who finished as the runner-up for the MVP award last season. The 24-year-old finished the contest 23 of 33, with 178 yards, a touchdown and three interceptions, all of which came in the fourth quarter. Maye also rushed for 47 yards.

In Maye's defense, he was hardly the only problem for the Patriots on Wednesday. The team's rushing attack was stopped at nearly every turn. Star wideout A.J. Brown was forced to leave the game due to an ankle injury and newcomer Romeo Doubs dropped what would have been a big play. Some also questioned Patriots offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels' approach, as the team couldn't handle or adjust to the Seahawks' blitzes.

Some of those struggles were due to a strong Seahawks defense. If Week 1 was any indication, the Seahawks are once again going to boast one of the most fearsome defenses in the league.

But it's not necessarily going to get easier for Maye and the Patriots moving forward. After playing an easy schedule last season, the Patriots face much harder competition this year. Following Week 1's loss, the team will play the Pittsburgh Steelers, Jacksonville Jaguars and Buffalo Bills in its next three games.

Those aren't easy wins, meaning Maye will have to get it together against strong competition if he hopes to shake off his Week 1 struggles.

item.title: De’Von Achane aiming for NFL rushing title, ready for Week 1
item.description: Miami Dolphins running back De’Von Achane expects a lot of himself this season.
item.content:encoded:
The Miami Dolphins are set to begin their 2026 NFL regular season on Sunday, kicking off a 17-game-over-18-week schedule. The analysts expect the Dolphins to struggle this season, with many predicting Miami to own the first-overall pick in the 2027 Draft by the time the season ends. The Dolphins, themselves, are not buying into those prognostications and are still setting lofty goals – especially running back De’Von Achane.

Miami’s 2023 third-round pick explained the importance of setting goals, saying, “I feel like you don’t got goals, I feel like what are you playing the game for? And you know, I kind of add more goals as we go through the season, but we always start with some.”

When asked to share one of his personal goals, Achane set a lofty objective. “I always try to go for the rushing title so that’s just something I do,“ he stated.

Achane, coming off his first career Pro Bowl selection, is expected to be the focal point of the offense this season. Head coach Jeff Hafley joked earlier in the summer that he would be looking to give Achane 45 touches per game this season. While 45 touches is not realistic, Achane was asked how many touches he thinks he will get in Sunday’s game against the Las Vegas Raiders. “I have no idea,” he replied. “I feel like, don’t nobody really know how many times you’re going to touch the ball. I feel like it’s just kind of a however the game is going type thing.”

With all the focus on Achane, opposing defenses will likely keep defenders close to the line of scrimmage to slow him down. Asked about what they would do to the offense, the running back recognized how that would open up the passing game, saying, “It just gives opportunities for our young receivers, or whoever’s out there, to make plays. Like you said, this is a team game. I can’t just go out there and win by myself. So when teams do stack the box, we can still try to run the ball, but if we have to adjust, it just gives opportunities for receivers to make plays.”

He continued, “It takes all of us. Just like they need me to run, I need them in the pass game. It goes both ways.”

The Dolphins underwent a coaching staff change this offseason, with former head coach and offensive play caller Mike McDaniel fired after the year ended and former Green Bay Packers defensive coordinator Jeff Hafley hired as the 12th full-time head coach in team history. Bobby Slowik, working as the passing game coordinator under McDaniel, was hired as the offensive coordinator for Hafley, keeping some stability in the offense while bringing a new perspective to the attack.

How will Slowick’s promotion impact Achane’s utilization? The fourth-year rusher said of the offense, “Of course it’s new…because it’s a new coach. So it’s kind of still the same, you add new stuff, but Slo was here last year with Mike, so some stuff is the same, some things are different. But at the same time, I feel like Slo uses me in the pass game, run game, so it’s good for me.”

Achane has lofty goals for himself this season and is probably going to have a great opportunity to reach them. But, in the near term, he is excited just to get the season started this weekend, saying, “I mean, it feels good, man. Like you said, it’s been a long time since we actually played four quarters, and I’ll been excited to be out there and just to go out there, just watch our team, to see how we come and basically just see how we hold up against somebody else for a full game.”

item.title: 5 bold Chiefs predictions from the Arrowhead Pride staff
item.description: These are the most extreme takes our staff has to offer about Kansas City football in 2026.
item.content:encoded:
They say fortune favors the bold.

The Kansas City Chiefs have certainly been bold through the years, from trading away veteran quarterback Alex Smith to start Patrick Mahomes to trading away All-Pro wide receiver Tyreek Hill in his prime. The organization has three Super Bowl trophies to show for it.

So now it’s time for the Arrowhead Pride staff to be bold. Here are five bold predictions about the Chiefs’ 2026 season:

Rocky Magana

The Chiefs hold opposing teams to under 280 yards from scrimmage per game.

For reference, this would put the Chiefs in the echelons of the Denver Broncos and Houston Texans in 2025. But with the addition of a young pass rusher like R Mason Thomas, and a blue chip cornerback in Masoor Delane (who I think will be a multi-time All Pro recipient in his career), along with the return of L’Jarius Sneed and the addition of Alohi Gillman, I think this defense takes the big step from being good, to great this season. I think the Chiefs are going to win a lot of one-score games this year, and the defense slamming the door shut on opponents will be the reason why.

Dakota Watson

For the first time since 2017, the Chiefs will have a 1,000-yard rusher AND receiver.

It is astounding that during the era of quarterback Patrick Mahomes, the Chiefs have never had a 1,000-yard rusher. That streak comes to an end with the signing of running back Kenneth Walker and with Mahomes coming off an injury, a (hopefully) more balanced attack. The last 1,000 yard rusher for the Chiefs was Kareem Hunt in 2017.

The bold part of this prediction, is that the Chiefs will also have one wide receiver attain 1,000 yards. The last Chiefs’ receiver to reach 1,000 yards was Tyreek Hill in 2021. It’s time for both these ugly streaks to come to an end.

Caleb James

The Chiefs will lead the NFL in rushing yards.

After multiple seasons of neglecting to develop running backs and putting a stunning lack of resources into acquiring them, the Chiefs signed the best free agent possible this offseason and also drafted a highly touted player.

The endgame? Run the damn ball.

Kenneth Walker showed the world a glimpse of who he can be in the playoffs this past season, and rookie running back Emmett Johnson has all the skills to develop into a star and to help the team hold a lethal one-two punch. This is what the interior of the offensive line was built for, and even with stability issues at tackle that could hurt the team in pass protection, Andy Reid is still savvy enough to scheme open runs as long as center Creed Humphrey and right guard Trey Smith blow open holes in the middle.

Walker should come close to leading the NFL in rushing yards, and Johnson should have a very productive rookie season. Look for Walker to go over 1,300 yards, and Johnson to come close to 800 on the ground.

Maurice Elston

The Chiefs will finish the season top 5 among NFL teams in interceptions

Kansas City recorded only 10 interceptions last season, ranking 22nd in the NFL, but its rebuilt secondary possesses greater ball-production potential.

Cornerbacks Nohl Williams and rookie Mansoor Delane have demonstrated strong ball skills. Williams tied for the Chiefs’ lead with seven passes defended as a rookie while earning a 75.6 PFF coverage grade and allowing completions on only 37.1% of his targets. In his final college season, he led the FBS with seven interceptions and recorded 16 passes defended.

Delane finished his final season at LSU with 13 passes defended, including 11 breakups and two interceptions, despite opponents rarely challenging him. The addition of safety Alohi Gilman also gives Kansas City a veteran safety with five career interceptions, compared with Bryan Cook’s three, while Chamarri Conner’s move into a more traditional safety role should create further opportunities.

Ron Kopp Jr.

Two Chiefs will finish in the top 5 of Defensive Rookie of the Year voting

In 2025, the Atlanta Falcons had two rookies finish within the top 5 of votes for the NFL AP Defensive Rookie of the Year award: edge rusher James Pearce and defensive back Xavier Watts.

I believe the Chiefs will have a similar duo finish within the top 5 this year: edge rusher R Mason Thoma and defensive back Mansoor Delane.

This bold prediction could have been centered around Thomas and his sack total. With Kansas City’s ability to stuff the run and set up pass-rush situations, I see Thomas taking advantage of playing with defensive tackle Chris Jones and closing in on 10 sacks in his first year.

However, his teammate on the boundary is going to take advantage of the revamped pass rush Thomas is leading. Delane looks the part of a physical cornerback that won’t be giving much room for completions on the outside. If he converts a handful of targets his way into highlight-reel interceptions, he and Thomas will both be vying for the award.

What’s your bold Chiefs prediction for the 2026 season? Let us know in the comments!

item.title: Evaluating Drake Maye’s season-opening performance
item.description: The former Tar Heel didn’t exactly look his best.
item.content:encoded:
The NFL season started with a Super Bowl rematch, and unfortunately for Tar Heels and Patriots fans, it was another rough outing for Drake Maye.

The third-year quarterback completed 23-of-33 passes for 178 yards with one touchdown and three interceptions as his team lost 13-10. 

In case you went to bed early (or were watching the US Open), Maye threw a 2-yard touchdown to Eli Raridon in the second quarter and led New England to a field goal on the opening drive of the third to go up 10-0. Things went downhill from there; the Patriots’ next four drives consisted of a three-and-out followed by three interceptions (meanwhile, Seattle put together three consecutive scoring drives to take the lead). The last interception is undoubtedly what people will be talking about today, as it came on a badly underthrown ball to the end zone with less than 30 seconds remaining.

What do you make of Maye’s performance? Do you think he was just unlucky to draw a defense that had his number seven months ago–and had plenty of time to prepare for him again–in the season opener? Or are you concerned there might be a letdown year coming?

Leave your thoughts in the comments below.

item.title: Our offense vs. their defense: Detroit Lions
item.description: Previewing the Saints’ offensive matchup in week 1
item.content:encoded:
Tyler Shough and the New Orleans Saints are finally set to begin their 2026 campaign on the road against the Detroit Lions this Sunday. After a relatively disappointing season that finished with a positive swing in momentum last year, expectations and vibes surrounding the team are now higher than they’ve been in over five years. Ahead of this weekend’s kickoff, let’s take a look at the offensive matchup for the Saints.

Detroit’s defense will be down a couple of key players in its secondary as CB Kerby Joseph and SS Brian Branch both landed on the injured reserve list, meaning each will be out at least the first four weeks of the season. The Lions’ defense had a down year in 2025 after giving up an average of over 330 yards per game.

Luckily for the Lions, DE Aidan Hutchinson is still an elite edge rusher and with Dan Campbell’s defensive background, the Michigan product should be able to make an impact in the backfield even if just hurrying the processing time of the offense.

Although the Saints will have limited options at the WR position available on Sunday due to injuries and roster cuts, Shough’s ability to build chemistry with his pass catchers early on could become a critical factor in New Orleans’ chances to steal a win in the Motor City. New Orleans’ initial depth chart for this weekend showed just three options at wideout to go along with the typical three tight ends.

New Orleans struggled to put points on the board last season, averaging just 18 per contest, a mark that ranked 28th in the league. Now, with a full offseason under their belts in the Big Easy, head coach Kellen Moore and Shough will seek to improve the team’s efficiency when in possession of the football, especially when inside of the redzone.

With new additions to the Saints such as RB Travis Etienne Jr., OL David Edwards, TE Noah Fant, and more, it is seemingly likely that New Orleans will find more success for their offensive production between the tackles. This, in turn, should allow other areas such as the play action passing game to open up further.

item.title: Post-Snap Reads: Seahawks grind out big win at home over the Patriots
item.description: The defense held serve, Drew Lock figured it out, and the defensive backfield put Drake Maye to bed.
item.content:encoded:
For several concrete reasons, your favorite team’s first game of an NFL season is always a bit messy, unpredictable, and usually is not an exact indicator of how the remainder of the schedule will play out. Bad teams look good early; good teams look bad early. Last night, our Seattle Seahawks endured an injury at a critical position, a slow start, penalties (lots of them), and a feisty New England Patriots squad to eek out a notable victory in their home/season opener. The defending champions found a way to win by pass rush, interceptions, and some nifty and timely play-calling from first time play-caller Brian Fleury. Jaxon Smith-Njigba, still disrespected despite winning OPOY last season, shouldered the weight of the offense to score a huge touchdown to tie the game late. Then, after Julian Love picked off Drake Maye (his second interception of the game), the Seahawks calmly marched down the the field, and despite themselves (a few odd procedural penalties, geez), kicked a FG to take the lead. From there, Coach Macdonald ratcheted up the Darkside and put enough pressure on the Pats to force Maye and Mike Vrabel into some bad decisions. item.title: Cowboys roundtable discussion: Cowboys vs Giants in Week 1
item.description: Here is our latest roundtable with a panel of BTB writers giving us their answers to this week’s questions
item.content:encoded:
Every week, we gather to discuss the latest news about the Dallas Cowboys and seek our writer’s perspective on each headline. Welcome back to the roundtable. This week we have Tom Ryle and Sean Martin. 

More important matchup: Cowboys interior defensive line vs Giants offensive line, or Cowboys offensive tackles vsGiants pass rush?

MIKE: The matchup that decides the game more is the Cowboys offensive tackles against the Giants pass rush. Dallas’ interior defensive line with Quinnen Williams and Kenny Clark should absolutely have chances to wreck the Giants’ protection, especially against a young quarterback, but the bigger swing factor is whether Tyler Guyton and Terence Steele can keep the edges clean for Dak Prescott.

SEAN: The Giants have been trying to sell their pass rush as their chip to win games forever, and nobody has bought it even once. I’m not about to start now, and even if the Cowboys tackles have their struggles, I think the Dallas offense can have enough quick game options or push in the run game to get by. 

The Cowboys interior defensive line against the Giants offensive line gets the nod for me here, especially since it’s already a spot many Cowboys fans will be keeping a close eye on, having not seen Quinnen Williams, Kenny Clark, or Otito Ogbonnia in the preseason. Especially if this group can push the pocket and get pressure on Jaxson Dart, the Cowboys will be in control of this game.

TOM: I’ll have to take the opposite position from Sean. As Mickey Spagnola said during a segment on a local radio show, the right tackle and swing tackle situations may be the biggest questions and most likely remaining holes for the team. I do have faith in Dak Prescott and the coaches to come up with a good game plan to attack the Giants, but I am not at all fond of the idea of our quarterback having to always be ducking and dodging. We all know what can happen if he, um, gets hit too much.

Conversely, I’m going to put my faith in the middle of the D line. After all, one of the accepted truths is that it is almost impossible for them to be worse than they were last year. Only one way to go.

Which young defender needs a big early statement, Caleb Downs, Shavon Revel, Jaishawn Barham, Donovan Ezeiruaku, or Malachi Lawrence?

MIKE: The player who needs to make the biggest early statement is Shavon Revel. Caleb Downs, Jaishawn Barham, Donovan Ezeiruaku and Malachi Lawrence all have exciting roles, but Revel’s spot feels the most important because cornerback is where one bad day can change the whole game plan. He is another year removed from his ACL injury now, so the excuses are over, and Dallas needs to know whether he can hold up outside without constant safety help.

SEAN: I’ll go with the biggest tweener of this group, rookie linebacker Jaishawn Barham. Everyone has been impressed by Barham’s combination of being stone cold and focused off the field, but determined like a heat seeking missile on it. How this translates to his first introduction into a regular season game, in primetime, against a rival that was a few plays away from sweeping the Cowboys a year ago, will be fun to watch, as well as just how much the Cowboys throw at him in these circumstances.

TOM: Well, this time I have to concur with Sean. There is a certain cyclical nature to the NFL, and we seem to be returning to the time when the middle linebackers are the engines of the defense. I just think Barham (or, as a friend of mine calls him, Barhammer) will have a bigger impact on more plays than any of the others. And if DeMarvion Overshown is healthy and back to his old self, this could be a truly dynamic duo.

After last year’s defensive collapse, what would count as real progress in Week 1?

MIKE: Real progress in Week 1 would not have to mean a shutout or a dominant stat line; it would mean the defense looks organised, physical, and trustworthy again. After last year’s collapse, Dallas needs to show cleaner communication, fewer busted coverages, better tackling in space, and a front that can stop the run without needing constant safety help. 

SEAN: Just playing assignment football. Offenses are going to make plays at this level and move the ball, but giving up layup throws like the Cowboys did all the time in 2025 is just too much to overcome. Force Jaxson Dart to think from the pocket by squeezing the Giants run game, don’t give up layups and dunks on the back end, and to pick up with something that was a plus in the preseason – continue defending well in the red zone.

TOM: Stop the run and don’t allow Jaxson Dart to convert long third downs. Last year’s edition of the defense failed at those two tasks so often last season. That has to stop, from the jump, for this team to fight its way back into the postseason.

RAPID FIRE

Who scores first for Dallas?

SEAN: Jake Ferguson

TOM: Javonte Williams at the end of a long, workmanlike drive

Dak Prescott passing yards, over/under 275.5?

SEAN: Under

TOM: Under, because I’m expecting them to lean on the ground game

CeeDee Lamb receptions, over/under 7.5

SEAN: Over

TOM: Under, for all the reasons I listed above

Quinnen Williams and Kenny Clark combined tackles for loss, over/under 3.5?

SEAN: Under

TOM: Under, but watch out for Barham

Who has the bigger night, CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens, or Jake Ferguson?

SEAN: George Pickens

TOM: Pickens. I think he is a man on a mission

Bigger defensive key, pressure Jaxson Dart or stop the run early?

SEAN: Stop the run early, and often

TOM: Definitely stop the run

More important, Dallas starts fast on offense or avoids early defensive busts?

SEAN: Avoid defensive busts that would instantly give the Giants, and their crowd, a boost of confidence.

TOM: Did you watch last season? The defense has to do better, and I expect the offense to take a couple or three series to get their rhythm

item.title: No snap count restrictions for Chris Bell in Dolphins opener
item.description: Miami’s rookie receiver will be a full-go against Raiders in week one.
item.content:encoded:
The Miami Dolphins may have struck gold when they nabbed wide receiver Chris Bell from Louisville in the third round of the 2026 NFL Draft. After all, the player was projected to be a late first round pick prior to his ACL tear in November of last year. Due to that injury, many thought that Bell would be eased back into action — possibly missing the first half of his rookie season. However, Bell’s recovery has been an expeditious one, and the receiver has been named a starter for the Dolphins ahead of their Week One clash in Las Vegas against the Raiders.

And according to new head coach Jeff Hafley, Bell will be a full-go and will not be on a snap count when he takes the field on Sunday.

Yesterday, while speaking with the South Florida media, Hafley confirmed that Bell will have no restrictions against Las Vegas.

“We’re going to play him — see how he feels — but, there’s no pitch count on Chris.”

Bell’s full availability is an extremely positive development for the Dolphins, especially this early in the season. Quarterback Malik Willis will have a full complement of weapons for his first start with Miami — including fellow rookies Caleb Douglas and Kevin Coleman Jr., as well as Malik Washington and tight end Greg Dulcich. Of course, Miami’s most explosive offensive player, De’Von Achane, will factor mightily into this tilt as well.

Will that be enough to allow Miami to sneak past Las Vegas? We will all find out in just a few short days.

item.title: What Will the 2026 Dolphins Passing Game Look Like? Let’s Ask the 2022–2023 Packers
item.description: Packers’ philosophy gives insight into how Dolphins receiver’s room may develop.
item.content:encoded:
The Packers built a passing game without a WR1 — and the Dolphins might do the same.

The Dolphins are heading into 2026 with one of the youngest receiver rooms in the league, with three rookies and a second‑year player expected to play real snaps – all catching passes from an unproven, first‑time starting quarterback. That might sound terrifying in the short term, but we actually have a modern template for how this can work: The Packers from 2022–2023, who rebuilt their pass‑catcher group while transitioning to Jordan Love.

The parallels are striking: A young quarterback stepping into a bigger role, a receiver room built almost entirely from scratch and a front office willing to bet on development. Jon‑Eric Sullivan helped architect Green Bay’s youth movement, drafting Christian Watson, Romeo Doubs, Jayden Reed, and Dontayvion Wicks in a two-year span, and now he’s trying to build the same long‑term payoff in Green Bay South.

So How Did It Pan Out in Green Bay?

Even early in the youth movement, Green Bay’s passing game was solid – which is perhaps to be expected when you have a first‑ballot Hall of Famer behind center. In 2022, Aaron Rodgers’ final season with the Packers, the team finished with 3,890 passing yards and 26 passing touchdowns. Fifteen different players caught passes, and eight of them topped 200 receiving yards. Among the rookies, Christian Watson finished second on the team with 611 yards and 7 touchdowns, while Romeo Doubs added 425 yards and 3 scores.

In 2023, with Jordan Love taking over, the passing numbers improved. Love threw for 4,159 yards and 32 touchdowns, and once again the ball was spread widely: sixteen players caught passes, and nine of them reached 200+ receiving yards. Reed, Doubs, Wicks, and Watson combined for roughly 2,500 yards and 25 touchdowns, but none eclipsed 800 yards – a sign that the Packers built the room around depth. (Incidentally, the trend continued beyond these transitional years. Reed and Doubs led the team in 2024 and 2025 with 857 yards and 724 yards, respectively, and six touchdowns apiece.)

What Might This Mean for Miami?

This isn’t apples to apples – Miami’s offense will look different. For one, the attack will likely run through De’Von Achane, who Jeff Hafley joked would get the ball 40–45 times per game. And Malik Willis brings a running element that Jordan Love didn’t, which will change how defenses play Miami.

But when Willis does throw, the distribution may look a lot like Green Bay’s. The Dolphins have six receivers on their 53‑man roster, plus Achane, pass‑catching tight end Greg Dulcich, and several other skill players who can handle targets. The Packers’ young receivers made an impact right away – Reed led the team in yards as a rookie – but at no point did they produce a traditional WR1 with 1,000 yards and double‑digit touchdowns. Miami’s passing game may follow the same pattern, with broad distribution, steady growth and no single player dominating the stat sheet.

Keep Expectations in Check

As much as we all might love a breakout 1,200‑yard receiver in Miami this season to replace the Cheetah and the Penguin, that might be setting us up for disappointment. But if you can live with a deep and versatile group that gets better as the year goes on – the Packers showed that’s absolutely possible. And with Jon‑Eric Sullivan now running Miami’s roster, it’s no coincidence the Dolphins are trying to build something similar.

item.title: Lions Week 1 preview: Breaking down Saints’ offensive, defensive schemes
item.description: Breaking down the offensive and defensive schemes of the New Orleans Saints, the Detroit Lions’ Week 1 opponent.
item.content:encoded:
The Detroit Lions and New Orleans Saints will square off in a Week 1 battle to open their 2026 seasons. The Saints hired former Lions backup quarterback Kellen Moore as head coach in 2025, and despite a rough first year, New Orleans and Moore made no changes to the coaching staff in year two. Instead, they focused on cohesion and upgrading their roster to improve the team.

Let’s take a closer look at the Saints’ coaching staff, the scheme they run, and some scouting notes from previously viewed games in 2025.

Saints head coach: Kellen Moore

NFL coaching seasons: Entering year two (2025-26)
Offensive coordinator: Cowboys (2019-22), Chargers (2023), Eagles (2024)
Influences: Scott Linehan, Mike McCarthy
Coached under: Jason Garrett, Mike McCarthy, Brandon Staley, Nick Sirianni
Playcaller: Yes
Detroit connection: Lions backup QB (2012-14)

Dan Campbell on Saints’ coaching staff:

“Kellen (Moore)’s done a good job; obviously, year two. There are still some guys that are there that I had a lot of respect for and that I think a lot of, (Offensive Line Coach) Brendan Nugent that I coached with. (Associate Head Coach/Running Backs Coach) Joel Thomas is back there. Those guys—I was with them—really good coaches.”

Offensive coordinator: Doug Nussmeier

NFL coaching seasons: 11 seasons
Offensive coordinator seasons: Entering year two (2025-26)
Previous coaching positions: QB coach: Eagles (2024), Chargers (2023), Cowboys (2020-22), Rams (2006-07); TE coach: Cowboys (2018-19)
Local college coaching spots: Michigan OC/QB coach (2014, under Brady Hoke), Michigan State QB coach (2003-05 under John L. Smith)
Influences: Scott Linehan, Kellen Moore, Mike McCarthy
Coached under (NFL): Jason Garrett, Mike McCarthy, Brandon Staley, Nick Sirianni, Kellen Moore
Coached under (College): Nick Saban, Jim McElwain, Steve Sarkisian
Detroit staff connection: Scott Linehan (Senior Offensive Assistant), Josh Hill (TE coach)

Offensive scheme

Passing game: Shotgun Spread-oriented (roughly 75%), RPOs (Think Eagles offense)
Running scheme: Outside Zone-based
Staples of scheme (data from 2025):

  • Moore built the scheme to fit the Saints players; has shown the ability to adapt in his past stops
  • You can see the influences from his time with the Eagles in the current Saints scheme
  • From shotgun: 70% pass/30% run split (under center it’s reversed)
  • Pass-heavy between the 20s (roughly 60-40 split), but closer to 50-50 in the red zone
  • Play-action is minimal: Just 18.4% last season (31st in the NFL)
  • QB Tyler Shough used PA just 18.6% of the time over his nine starts
  • Sacks allowed as a team: 49 (2.88 per game)
  • Sacks allowed by Shough in nine starts: 29 (3+ sacks per game)
  • Pressures allowed by team: 227 (13.4 per game)
  • Pressures on Shough: 119 (13.22 per game)
  • Yards per rush in each blocking scheme: Zone (3.85+ ypc), Gap/Power (2.8 ypc)

Dan Campbell on QB Tyler Shough:

“There’s a level of maturity, composure that you see that looks like that’s here to stay.”

Dan Campbell on Saints’ offense:

“They have got some potency: (WR Chris) Olave and (RB Travis) Etienne, (TE) Juwan (Johnson), I like this O-line. I think it’s a talented offensive line.”

More on Johnson (Campbell was his position coach before joining the Lions):

“He’s a big skilled player, a mismatch player. The things where he stays on the move keep him vertical. He’s got range, he’s got length, he can track the ball. So, it’s comes a long way, but I think that was always the vision for him. So, I’m not surprised where he’s gone because I know when I was there young, it was like, ‘Man, this kid may be able to develop into a receiving threat as a tight end slot.’ And he’s been able to do that.”

Defensive coordinator: Brandon Staley

NFL coaching seasons: 10 seasons
Defensive coordinator seasons: Entering year three; Rams (2020), Saints (2025-26)
Previous roles: Head Coach: Chargers (2021-23); Assistant head coach/defense: 49ers (2024); LB coach: Bears (2017-18), Broncos (2019)
Influences: Vic Fangio
Coached under: John Fox, Matt Nagy, Vic Fangio, Sean McVay, Kyle Shanahan
Detroit staff connection: Bo Davis (DL coach)

Dan Campbell on Staley:

“Brandon (Staley) came in, brought their system in and really didn’t miss a beat. It’s a good defense, man. They play hard.”

Jared Goff (who worked opposite Staley in LA) on hallmarks of his defense:

“Very sound. Good communicators. Everything looks the same, but it’s different. Play hard. Yeah, they’re tough, I mean all that. They were good in LA and certainly they were good when I was with him in LA and then with the Chargers and they’re good again there.”

Defensive scheme

Base: 3-4 Base, gap-and-a-half front
Coverage: Vic Fangio zone-match principles; loads of Cover-3 (roughly 50% of the time, most in the NFL)
Staples of scheme:

  • 2025 was a redemption year for Staley
  • Learned from the mistake of leaning too much into deploying Fangio’s exact defense with the Chargers; realized he needed to be more adaptable to personnel with the Saints
  • Kept split zone/two-high safety looks, but shifted away from heavy-nickel
  • Ran 4th-ranked “Base” defense in the NFL in 2025
  • Cover-3 (50%), Cover-4 (17%), Cover-6 (10%), Cover-1 Man (15%)
  • Blitz Rate: 16% (21st); very situational
  • DVOA run defense: 8th (potential hurdle: LB Demario Davis departed in free agency)
  • 3rd-down conversion percentage allowed: 34.3% (third best)
  • While the offensive personnel was upgraded this offseason, the defense filled gaps
  • Three second-year players are starting due to departures in free agency or injury (i.e., Bryan Breese is on IR and replaced by Vernon Broughton), though two of those players in the secondary (CB Quincy Riley and NB/S Jonas Sanker) got a lot of experience last season.
  • EDGE Cameron Jordan has been ruled OUT

Dan Campbell on Saints’ defense:

“(DE) Chase Young’s playing the best football he’s played. We’ll see if (DE Cameron) Cam (Jordan) plays. I think we all know what Cam Jordan is. I think (DE Carl) Granderson’s a really good player up front. And then those backers, (LB Kaden) Elliss and (LB Pete) Werner—and (CB Kool-Aid) McKinstry is playing pretty good in the boundary. So, look, it’s a good unit.”

item.title: ESPN gives an update on a Tucker Kraft extension
item.description: Green Bay wants a deal done by the end of Week 1, according to Jeremy Fowler
item.content:encoded:
Jeremy Fowler dropped a long Week 1 buzz article for ESPN on Thursday morning, and it included some nuggets on where the Green Bay Packers and tight end Tucker Kraft stand on an extension. In the past, general manager Brian Gutekunst stated that he wanted a Kraft deal done going into the regular season, but there is no deal in place yet.

Here’s what Fowler had to say about the situation:

This summer has featured complete market resets at cornerback and defensive tackle, and tight end could be next. It’s the only offensive or defensive position without a player making $20 million or more per season, but the Packers’ Tucker Kraft is hoping to change that. He remains in discussions about a new contract, but it has been a bit of a standoff so far. Green Bay hopes to get something done by the end of Week 1, so perhaps urgency prevails here. If Kraft can get a deal above that $20 million threshold, that sets the stage for Detroit’s Sam LaPorta. The Lions have interest in extending him, but his situation might carry into the season.

$20 million per year might sound like a lot for a tight end, but it’s really not that big of a jump from where the position is at right now. As we wrote after the Kyle Pitts extension, here are the four highest-paid tight ends in the league from an average-per-year perspective:

  • George Kittle: $19.1 million per
  • Trey McBride: $19 million per
  • Kyle Pitts: $18 million per
  • Isaiah Likely: $13.3 million per

Once Pitts signed for $18 million per year, it was assumed that Kraft would receive more than him. The only question was whether he was going to get paid in line with George Kittle and Trey McBride or truly become the highest-paid tight end in the league, despite him coming off an ACL tear. At least according to Fowler, Kraft’s camp is eyeing to “reset” the tight end market, even if the ceiling at the position rises by only about a million dollars per year.

Fowler is also correct in that Sam LaPorta is the other tight end situation to pay attention to, as he’s the only other significant tight end going into a contract year in 2026. With Pitts off the table, it’s the Kraft and LaPorta show, as far as tight end extensions go. A big question is who will be first to sign, and whether or not the second player’s number will rise to try to beat the first’s benchmark.

item.title: Patriots express confidence in Drake Maye after Seahawks loss
item.description: The third-year quarterback threw three costly picks on Wednesday night.
item.content:encoded:
The New England Patriots see Drake Maye as the face of their franchise. On Wednesday night, he was relegated to being the face of their defeat.

Going up against the same Seattle Seahawks team that beat him and his team in Super Bowl LX seven months earlier, the third-year quarterback played one of the worst games of his career. Maye threw interceptions on each of the Patriots’ final three possessions, playing a critical part in a 10-0 lead turning into a 13-10 defeat.

Maye himself was critical of his performance, calling the three picks “unacceptable” during his postgame press conference. The rest of his team, meanwhile, was not that harsh on the 24-year-old.

“We have nothing but the utmost confidence in him and everybody on this football team,” said head coach Mike Vrabel. “He’s going to make a lot of plays for us.”

Maye did just that on Sunday, even after his interception woes began. Following his first two picks, which allowed Seattle to take a lead for the first time all day, he marched the Patriots into the red zone on what very well could have been the game-winning drive.

Along the way, he showed his trademark playmaking ability as both a passer and a runner. However, that series, like the two previous ones, ended with a costly mistake by the former third overall draft pick.

And yet, his teammates made sure not to pin the defeat on Maye.

“It’s not on one person at all,” said running back Rhamondre Stevenson. “This is a team game. We win together and we lose together. I wouldn’t pinpoint on one single person in that room. We all have to get better. Back to the drawing board and figure it out.”

“I have the utmost confidence in him,” added wide receiver Romeo Doubs, the target on the first of Maye’s three INTs. “I know what he can do. I’ve watched him and what he’s done in this league a long time, and, like I said, this doesn’t define him. It’s just this league, it’s always a pendulum in this league.”

The message of support did not only come out of the offense. The Patriots defense echoed those remarks as well.

“We have all the confidence in the world in Drake,” said cornerback Carlton Davis. “He’s our guy. We are going to stick together right now, and we’ll move forward.”

item.title: Chris Brooks could decide the Packers’ Week 1 matchup against Minnesota
item.description: Green Bay’s most impactful running back on Sunday might be Chris Brooks, as a blocker
item.content:encoded:
One of the more underrated matchups going into the Green Bay Packers’ regular-season opener against the Minnesota Vikings, at least to me, is how running back Chris Brooks will do against defensive coordinator Brian Flores’ blitz-heavy front. The Packers have said that they will be trying out a running back-by-committee approach early on in the season, but I want to talk about blocking, not ball-carrying, when it comes to what Brooks can bring to the table.

Everyone and their mother knows that Flores wants to blitz. It’s in his DNA. It’s who he has been, who he is and who he will want to be in the future.

Arguably, Packers head coach Matt LaFleur’s best trait as a coach has been his team’s pass-rushing plans, as there have been few players up front who have been allowed to take over games, even when the team has matched up against the Aaron Donalds, Myles Garretts and Aidan Hutchinsons of the world.

His line gets a lot of chip help from tight ends, funky spacing that puts rushers in bad positions pre-snap and running backs who add on to the protection. That’s where Brooks had thrived in the past.

Below is a clip from Week 1 last year, where Brooks, against a mugged-up Detroit Lions front, passes off a linebacker and takes on a defensive tackle on a stunt to allow Jordan Love to make a big throw in the middle of the field. Yes, a defensive tackle.

Last year, PFF graded Brooks as the fourth-best running back league-wide in pass protection. To make this short and simple: He’s a really good blocking back.

I’d expect that the Packers will want to lean into Brooks’ blocking ability, especially on obvious passing downs, against Flores’ aggressive scheme. Especially when three of Green Bay’s starting offensive linemen are currently on the injury report and were limited during Wednesday’s practice.

So don’t discount Brooks being a difference-maker in the Week 1 matchup, even if he’s not going to receive the bulk of the carries out of the backfield. It also probably helps the Packers that they just signed safety Kahlef Hailassie, who was with the Vikings for all of training camp and was just released two days ago, to their practice squad. Teams usually spend two weeks of game planning for their Week 1 opponent, rather than one, because they receive that extra week between cutdowns and the start of the regular season.

Maybe Hailassie knows a little about the pass-rush plan that Flores has for the Packers and had installed over the last week, and he’ll want to share that with Brooks. You’ve got to love a little gamesmanship.

item.title: Rams get under salary cap with Quentin Lake contract move
item.description: Rams make a necessary move to get “under” the cap
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Rams have created some much-needed salary-cap flexibility by restructuring the contract of defensive back Quentin Lake, freeing approximately $3.4 million in 2026 cap space.

According to the terms of the restructure, the Rams converted $4.285 million of Lake’s salary into a signing bonus. The team then added two void years to the end of his contract, allowing Los Angeles to spread the cap charge from the bonus beyond the current length of the deal.

The move comes just months after the Rams made a significant commitment to Lake. Los Angeles signed the versatile defensive back to a three-year contract extension on Jan. 1, 2026. The deal keeps Lake under contract through 2028 and reportedly includes $25.5 million in guarantees.

Lake has become an important piece of the Rams’ defense because of his versatility, having the ability to play safety while also contributing in the slot. His emergence made him a logical player for the Rams to retain long term. Now, the Rams are using his contract to create additional financial flexibility.

Following the restructure, Los Angeles is approximately $2.8 million under the 2026 salary cap after previously sitting slightly above the limit. The extra room could prove valuable as the Rams navigate the final stages of roster construction, make potential additions or prepare for future moves.

However, the decision to restructure Lake’s contract is notable for another reason: the Rams had other players they could have used to create cap space, but chose Lake instead.

Kevin Dotson immediately stands out. Dotson is entering the final year of his three-year, $48 million contract with Los Angeles, which he signed in 2024. His current deal carries a significant 2026 cap number, and he has emerged as one of the more important pieces of the Rams’ offensive line.

A further extension for Dotson could have potentially created immediate cap relief while also securing an important offensive lineman beyond 2026. Instead, the Rams have not extended him at this point.

item.title: Drake Maye’s 3-interception night has Patriots fans worried about one word
item.description: Three interceptions from Drake Maye has Patriots fans worried about one word
item.content:encoded:
After the New England Patriots made a dream run to Super Bowl LX, New England Patriots fans entered the 2026 season hoping for something even bigger in the year ahead.

With the acquisition of A.J. Brown, as well as additions along the offensive line and elsewhere, there were hopes that the team could take a step forward, and prove that last season was not a fluke. But there was one word in the back of every Patriots fan’s mind, one that might give them a little pause before the season began.

And that word might be at the front of their minds right now.

Regression.

Certainly there was fear that the team could take a step back, given that instead of facing a schedule with a winning percentage of .391 — the lowest a team faced while advancing to a Super Bowl — but specifically from quarterback Drake Maye. Against that schedule a season ago, Maye played himself into MVP consideration, thanks to a combination of success when pushing the ball downfield, and an ability to avoid costly mistakes. Maye led the NFL in several statistical categories, including Yards per Attempt (8.9), Adjusted Yards per Attempt (9.5), QBR (77.5), Net Yards Per Attempt (7.8), and Adjusted Yards per Attempt (8.3).

He did that while throwing just eight interceptions all year.

But on opening night in Seattle, he threw three, including one that he called “unacceptable,” a turnover that ended any chance of a New England win.

The first was a classic example of a quarterback trying to do too much. New England had a 10-3 lead early in the fourth quarter and faced 2nd and 9 at the Seattle 45-yard line. Working off of play-action, Maye has a deep curl route from Mack Hollins and a vertical route from Romeo Doubs to choose from.

He tries to hit the vertical route, forcing a throw — an underthrown one at that — into coverage that is tipped and intercepted:

Speaking after the game, Maye called this play an example of not being “patient” as a quarterback:

Oh, definitely. I just stopped being patient. I think that’s the big thing. We were really good up to the point where I tried to force one down the sideline to Romeo [Doubs], where we were patient and dumping it off and trying to move the chains. And we avoided a lot of 3-and-outs, and that was something we try to just earn more plays in the explosive. So, just stopped being patient and made decisions that ended up, like I said, that cost us the game.

(Transcript provided by PatsFans.com).

Seattle tied the game on their ensuing possession, and the Patriots did not help themselves on their next drive, as an illegal block penalty on the kickoff saw New England start the drive on their own 10-yard line. While they picked up a first down, they faced 3rd-and-14 on their own 22-yard line a few plays later.

Enter interception number two:

The Patriots dial up a vertical concept, with go routes to the outside from Mack Hollins and Doubs, with another vertical route from Pop Douglas in the slot. Seattle drops into a Cover 6 look here, with the Cover 2 side over the combination of Douglas and Doubs, and the Cover 4 side to Hollins.

While Douglas and Maye do not seem on the same page, the bigger problem might be Maye’s eyes. As you can see from the end zone angle, he gives the route to Douglas a long look, leading safety Julian Love right to the football.

Despite those two mistakes, the Patriots still had a chance to salvage the night with a win. Following this second interception, New England’s defense held Seattle to a field goal to make it a 13-10 game, and the Patriots had just under six minutes to retake the lead, or at least force overtime.

New England moved right into field goal range, converting a 4th-and-2 at one point on a bootleg from Maye to extend the drive. After a Rhamondre Stevenson run picked up eight yards and moved New England down to the Seattle 28-yard line, the Seahawks burned their final timeout, giving New England full control of the clock.

But with just 26 seconds remaining, and the Patriots facing 3rd-and-5 at the Seattle 16-yard line, this happened:

We’ll get to Maye’s decision in a moment, but full credit to DeMarcus Lawrence on the edge. New England was asking tackles Will Campbell and Morgan Moses to cut block on the edges often, as a way of slowing down the Seattle pass rush. Lawrence hurdles Moses and then stays in perfect position, keeping Maye in the pocket and pressuring him into making a decision.

A poor one at that. Maye said as much after the loss:

Yeah, I think we had the game under control. I thought we had a good plan to try to start chipping away and be patient. And I lost patience, and it cost us. I think it’s just decisions that cost us the game, on my part and my end. And I vowed to myself to be better and realize it’s a long season, but at the same time, you can’t have those. You can’t have those. And it’s unacceptable. And I know that I’ve got to get back to work because that wasn’t how I play football and how I want to represent my game and playing quarterback for the Patriots.

Maye then discussed the final play:

Yeah, it was something where we had a certain protection on where we were cutting, and I was trying to get rid of it and realized we were – Mack was back there in the back and didn’t put enough on it to get it out. And it was just unacceptable. We had a chance to send it to overtime at the worst. And the only thing you can do is turn the ball over. And that’s what I did.

With the third interception, Maye finished the night having completed 23-of-33 passes for 178 yards, a touchdown, and three interceptions. While it was not all bad — he made some big plays with his legs and, until the fourth quarter at least, seemed to have answers for Seattle’s defense — those three interceptions are the headline.

One Week 1 loss does not make a season, and the Patriots know this as well as anyone. Last year began with an underwhelming 20-13 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders, a team that went on to secure the first-overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.

But the Patriots have games against three AFC playoff hopefuls over the next three weeks: The Pittsburgh Steelers, the Jacksonville Jaguars, and the Buffalo Bills. And the version of Maye we saw Wednesday night in Seattle, the impatient version, could struggle against those teams as well.

One game does not a season make, but Wednesday night’s loss does have Patriots fans thinking about that one word.

Regression.

item.title: Cam Heyward voices displeasure with franchise tag
item.description: Cam Heyward sounds off on the use of the franchise tag.
item.content:encoded:
Pittsburgh Steelers defensive tackle Cam Heyward dealt with his own contract dispute before agreeing to a contract sweetener before the 2025 season.

Joey Porter Jr. finds himself in a similar predicament, looking for a new deal before the Steelers take the field against the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday. Porter is due to make just under $4 million in the final year of his rookie contract.

Top corners Devon Witherspoon (Seahawks) and Christian Gonzalez (Patriots) have reset the core back market with deals exceeding $100 million guaranteed. 

One angle the Steelers could take with Porter Jr., if they don’t agree on a deal, is to place the franchise tag on him and retain his rights for 2027. Porter Jr. would earn $24 million, a $20 million raise but less than the projected $27-30 million he could earn with a long-term contract.  The longest-tenured Steeler thinks the franchise tag is pointless for players and shouldn’t be eligible to be used in the league. 

“It’s stupid,” Heyward said after practice. “It hampers players. Why should any team be able to take advantage of a player for one year?”

The Steelers signed 2023 draft picks Nick Herbig, Darnell Washington, and Keeanu Benton to deals, leaving Porter Jr. as the lone remaining contributor. 

“It’s used in negotiations, and I think between the player options, the franchise tags, the way they control rookies, I think it’s kind of backwards,” Heyward said.

The Steelers put a team policy in place during the 1990s that they would not negotiate with players in season, meaning only days remain for Porter Jr. and the franchise to agree to terms. There is still time, and negotiations can change in a dime. NFL Network reporter Mike Garafolo said on Tuesday that the Steelers have made an offer to Porter Jr., but the two sides remain far apart.

item.title: How the Broncos can defeat the Chiefs on Monday Night Football
item.description: Here are three things the Denver Broncos must do to defeat the Kansas City Chiefs on Monday Night Football.
item.content:encoded:
After an impressive 14-win season in 2025, the Denver Broncos are the reigning AFC West champions. They dethroned the Kansas City Chiefs from that spot, who endured their worst season in a decade last year. The Broncos’ quest at a second straight AFC West title and subsequent Super Bowl chase begins on Monday Night Football at Arrowhead Stadium.

The Broncos’ offense has to start off fast

There are a lot of reasons to be optimistic about the Broncos in 2026. Nevertheless, one order of business must be achieved. That’s going from a middle-of-the-pack offense to a Top 10-unit in the National Football League.

This season will be Bo Nix’s third year leading the offense and Offensive Coordinator Davis Webb’s first season calling plays for Denver. I’m bullish on what the two can accomplish and believe Nix is poised for his best year of his career. However, the Broncos must start off fast and forego their early seasons woes that have plagued the group’s efficiency and productivity in the first part of the past two seasons.

On the road against the Chiefs, they face a formidable defense coached by Steve Spagnuolo. He does a great job dialing up pressure and confusing opposing quarterbacks. Kansas City used a lot of draft selections to bolster that side of the ball and ended up revamping a good portion of their secondary.

With the addition of Jaylen Waddle, the Broncos have a premier playmaker in the mix that was absent from last year’s gridiron campaign. Getting Waddle, the ball and creating some explosive plays through the air will be mission critical to achieve victory. I’m hopeful Denver will be able to get him involved to boost their aerial attack and dial up some big plays against a revamped Chiefs secondary.

The Broncos’ defense has to find a way to rattle Patrick Mahomes; slow down Kenneth Walker III

Even with Patrick Mahomes coming off a down year that ended prematurely due to an ACL tear, the Broncos defense can’t underestimate his top-notch playmaking ability. In order to defeat the Chiefs, Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph is going to have to dial up the heat on Mahomes and force him into some bad decisions.

Left tackle Josh Simmons may be sidelined from the game due to injury. If that happens, at least one of the Chiefs’ starting tackle spots will be manned by an undrafted rookie free agent. That may be just enough of an opportunity for Nik Bonitto and the rest of Denver’s front seven to feast and cause some havoc.

Additionally, the Broncos have to find a way to slow down running back Kenneth Walker III. He is coming off a great season and was the Seattle Seahawks’ Super Bowl MVP last year. Setting the tempo and pace of the game is important, and finding a way to shut down Andy Reid’s ground game plans will be essential to earn a Week 1 win.

Play disciplined football and win the turnover battle

There were two major issues that were prevalent last year with the Broncos. They were the fourth most penalized team in football and ranked toward the bottom of the league in forcing turnovers. Knowing that, it’s quite impressive they managed to reel off 14 wins and advance to the AFC Championship Game.

This season, things have to be different on both fronts. Last year, too many drives on offense stalled or were extended for the opposition with penalties and miscues. If they can cut down on those, the Broncos should be even tougher to defeat in ‘26. The Chiefs are already a tough opponent as is, they can’t make things harder for themselves by shooting themselves in the foot.

In ‘25, the Broncos sported a -4 turnover differential. They were one of only a handful of teams to make the playoffs being in the negative. All offseason long, the coaching staff and players emphasized how essential it will be to turn the tides in that regard. Late last season and in the AFC Divisional Playoff victory over the Bills, we saw significant improvement with that. Hopefully, they can find a way to no
